collection: NECO BECE Basic Science and Technology JSS 3 practice
note: Original objective practice. Historical JSS 3 topic mapping and four-option classroom format are provisional. Current NECO objectives and NERDC adoption remain unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Use evidence to link the production of sound to vibration.
questions.prompt: After tapping a metal tray, Halima hears it ring. When she presses her palm gently against it, the sound stops sooner. Which explanation best fits the result?
options: Her palm makes sound travel faster through the room.
Her palm reduces the tray’s vibration.
Her palm increases the tray’s vibration.
Her palm makes the air denser throughout the room.
questions.answer: Her palm reduces the tray’s vibration.
questions.explanation: Contact with the hand damps the tray’s vibration, so it produces less sound.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Predict which surface treatment will reduce reflected sound.
questions.prompt: People hear repeated sound clearly in an empty hall. The school can cover part of a hard wall. Which covering is most likely to reduce the reflected sound?
questions.explanation: Thick fabric absorbs more of the sound than the hard, smooth surfaces, leaving less energy to reflect.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Identify the part of the ear that starts vibrating when sound reaches the end of the ear canal.
questions.prompt: A learner traces sound through a model of the ear. Which part at the inner end of the ear canal vibrates when sound arrives?
questions.explanation: Changes in air pressure travel along the ear canal and cause the eardrum to vibrate.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose the effect of an open switch in a single circuit path.
questions.prompt: Two working lamps and a switch are connected to a battery in one loop. The switch is opened between the lamps. What happens?
options: Only the lamp nearest the positive terminal goes out.
Only the lamp nearest the negative terminal goes out.
questions.explanation: Opening the switch breaks the only conducting path, so neither lamp receives current.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a fuse responds to excessive current.
questions.prompt: A pupil examines a diagram of a circuit that includes a fuse. What is the purpose of the thin metal element inside the fuse?
options: To store charge for later use.
To melt if the current is too large and break the circuit.
To cool the circuit whenever the current rises.
To reverse the direction of the current.
questions.answer: To melt if the current is too large and break the circuit.
questions.explanation: Excessive current heats the fuse element until it melts, opening the circuit.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Use successive cumulative meter readings to find energy used.
questions.prompt: A school electricity meter reads 2,540 kWh on Monday and 2,587 kWh the next Monday. The meter was not reset. How much electrical energy was used between the readings?
questions.explanation: A cumulative meter records energy used so far. Subtract the earlier reading from the later reading.
